card.text: A brown dwarf of 67 Jupiter masses, one of a pair orbiting far out around the nearby star Epsilon Indi A.

introduction.text: Epsilon Indi Ba is a brown dwarf 1,460 au from Epsilon Indi A. With Bb, a second brown dwarf, it circles a common centre every 11 years.

sources.label: Scholz et al. 2003
sources.quote: as a common proper motion companion (separation 1459AU) to the K5V star Epsilon Indi

sources.label: McCaughrean et al. 2004
sources.quote: We find it to be a close binary
